recommendation.answer: Concrete fix: Deploy Strict CSP with script-src 'nonce-{RANDOM}' 'strict-dynamic'. Nonces are unique one-time-use random values generated for each HTTP response. 'strict-dynamic' trusts those elements without explicitly adding nonces or hashes. When inline scripts are required, script-src hash allows only specific scripts. Preventing the page from executing inline scripts mitigates injecting <script>.

finding.description: Dans votre en-tête Content-Security-Policy, ajoutez une directive connect-src listant uniquement vos propres API et services de confiance (jamais '*' ni un schéma nu comme https:).

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: weak-csp-connect-src (Dans votre en-tête Content-Security-Policy, ajoutez une directive connect-src listant uniquement vos propres API et services de confiance (jamais '*' ni un schéma nu comme https:). Evidence: Votre site peut envoyer des données vers n'importe quel serveur sur internet : si un code pirate s'exécute sur votre page, il peut transmettre les saisies de vos visiteurs à un serveur inconnu sans laisser de trace.). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Fix: In your Content-Security-Policy header, add a restrictive connect-src allowlist containing only your own origins and trusted APIs, e.g. Content-Security-Policy: connect-src 'self' https://api.example.com wss://api.example.com. Never use '*' and never use a bare scheme like https:. This blocks exfiltration via fetch(), XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource and sendBeacon() to arbitrary servers.

sources.contribution: The HTTP Content-Security-Policy (CSP) connect-src directive restricts the URLs which can be loaded using script interfaces.
The following APIs are controlled by this directive: fetch(), XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, Navigator.sendBeacon()

By injecting the Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers from the server, the browser is aware and capable of protecting the user from dynamic calls that will load content into the page currently being visited.
